SMTO-MAN-0004 — That link to the SMTO Manual isn't valid

GUID: 026fc29b-e7b0-5002-9466-e40833727473
Slug: docs-invalid-ref
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: docs

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to open a Manual page with a reference it doesn't recognize, such as a mistyped, shortened or made-up link. Nothing was opened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If this appeared in a task's activity, ask SMTO to search its Manual for the topic first and use a page from those results. Manual references must exactly match one SMTO lists; a guessed reference is rejected.
  2. If you opened a Manual link yourself, copy it again in full from where you found it, without editing or shortening it. Even a small change, like a missing part or extra spaces, makes the reference invalid.

What success looks like

  • The Manual page opens, or SMTO quotes the page you asked about.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and say where the Manual link came from. Don't keep retrying the same link; it will fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • parse_ref rejected the Manual reference: it is not a string, exceeds 260 characters, lacks the manual:// prefix, or has a non-canonical document ID or heading.

What this means

  • parse_ref receives a non-string, more than 260 characters or a value without the manual:// prefix. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • parse_ref receives a non-string, more than 260 characters or a value without the manual:// prefix.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the complete value with a reference returned by docs.search or docs.list.

How to fix it

  • Use an exact manual:// reference returned by docs.search or docs.list (a canonical document ID plus an optional #heading ID, at most 260 characters). Do not construct or guess references; check the caller or citation that produced the malformed value.
  • Copy an exact manual:// reference returned by docs.search or docs.list.

Retry and execution caution

  • Copy an exact manual:// reference returned by docs.search or docs.list.

How to verify the fix

  • An exact returned manual:// reference parses successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not invent references, read arbitrary files through Docs or retry in a tight loop.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
